name: Rueda
terms: Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.
keyfacts: Rueda is a Spanish DO in Castile and León, known mainly for white wines based on the Verdejo grape.
The vineyards sit on a flat high plain at about 2,300 to 2,850 feet, with the Duero River forming its northern edge.
The climate is continental with some Atlantic influence, with long cold winters, late spring frosts and hot, dry summers.
Drip irrigation now helps vines cope with the hot, dry summers.
Gran Vino de Rueda comes from vineyards over 30 years old, with yields of at most 6,500 kg/ha and a juice extraction rate of at most 65%.

notes: Rueda Verdejo must be at least 85% Verdejo.

blurb.text: A Castile and León DO across 74 municipalities in Valladolid, Segovia and Ávila, known mainly for white wines from the Verdejo grape. Sauvignon Blanc, Macabeo and Palomino Fino are also allowed.
